title: Pistachio-Crusted Rack of Lamb
summary: Rack of lamb under a fragrant herb and pistachio crust. Quick to cook and impressive on the plate, for a special dinner. Serve with mashed potatoes and grilled asparagus.

steps.text: In a bowl, mix the pistachios, breadcrumbs, Parmigiano, sage, rosemary, thyme, mint and lemon zest. Stir in {@oil:amount*2/3} of the olive oil until the mixture holds together, and season with salt and pepper.
Season the rack of lamb generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining {@oil:amount*1/3} of olive oil in an ovenproof frying pan over a high heat. Sear the lamb on all sides until golden brown, {timer:2} per side. Take off the heat.
Brush the meat side of the lamb (not the bones) generously with the Dijon mustard.
Press the pistachio and herb mixture firmly onto the mustard to form a thick crust.
Put the pan in the oven, or move the lamb to a roasting tray. Roast for {timer:18} for medium-rare (52–55 °C inside).
Take out of the oven, cover loosely with foil and rest for {timer:8-10}.
Slice between the ribs into cutlets. Serve straight away with mashed potatoes and grilled asparagus.

tips: Ask your butcher to french the rack (clean the rib bones) for a neater presentation. The mustard glues the crust on and adds a tangy flavour. Do not skip the searing: it adds flavour and helps the crust stick. For medium-rare lamb, aim for 52–55 °C inside; it keeps cooking as it rests. The crust should be golden and fragrant. Save any crust that falls off to sprinkle over the plates. Mint sauce or a red wine jus makes a classic accompaniment.
